Estimated tax is the method used to pay tax on income that isn’t subject to withholding, including self-employment income [4.23]. 

You don’t have to pay estimated tax for 2026 if you meet all three of the following conditions:

- You were a U.S. citizen or resident alien for the whole year [4.24].

You also don’t have to pay estimated tax if you will pay enough through withholding to keep the amount you owe with your return under $1,000 [4.30].

If you do need to make estimated tax payments, when you must start and make your installments depends on when you first have income on which you must pay estimated tax [4.28]:
- **Before April 1:** First payment due April 15; later installments due June 15, September 15, and January 15 of the next year [4.28].
- **April 1–May 31:** First payment due June 15; later installments due September 15 and January 15 of the next year [4.28].
- **June 1–Aug. 31:** First payment due September 15; later installment due January 15 of the next year [4.28].
- **After Aug. 31:** First and only payment due January 15 of the next year [4.28].

*(Note: Payment due dates are subject to the Saturday, Sunday, and holiday rule and the January payment rule) [4.28].*
